change.title: pr-37038-flat
change.description: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: V2 canManage() grants manage on the VIEW scope
findings.body:
`canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. An admin whose all-groups permission has only the `view` scope therefore passes `canManage()`.

The no-arg `canManage()` is what `GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup` checks (`auth.groups().requireManage()`, GroupsResource.java:181). A view-only admin can create top-level groups. If the body carries an existing `id`, the endpoint also moves that group to top level (GroupsResource.java:192-199).

`canView()` at line 52 is the call that should use `VIEW, MANAGE`. `canManage()` should use only `MANAGE`, like `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79.

The javadoc in GroupPermissionEvaluator (lines 72-77) says `canManage()` is true for VIEW or MANAGE. It documents the bug and should change with the fix.

`testViewGroups` never checks that a view-only admin is denied a write, so no test catches this.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns resource UUIDs, not group ids
findings.body:
The lambda passes `groupResource.getId()` to `hasPermission(...)` and adds the same value to `granted`. In V2 the resource name is the group id: `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates it with `resourceStore.create(server, name, ...)` where name is `group.getId()`. The resource's own id is a different generated UUID. `ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission` correctly adds `resource.getName()`.

Two consequences:
1. `hasPermission(groupId, ...)` runs `resourceStore.findByName(server, <resource UUID>)`, which returns null. It then falls back to the all-groups type resource. With only per-group permissions it returns false, so `granted` stays empty. With an all-groups view-members permission, every group resource passes and `granted` holds UUIDs.
2. `UsersResource` and `BruteForceUsersResource` put this set in `UserModel.GROUPS` and `getUsersCount`. An empty set makes `JpaUserProvider.getUsersCount(..., groupIds)` return 0 (JpaUserProvider.java:600, 635, 683). A set of UUIDs matches no group membership.

So `GET /users/count` returns 0 for a group-scoped admin. The search runs unrestricted and `first/max` apply before the per-user `canView` post-filter, so a page can come back short or empty. With an all-groups permission the group-restricted search can return nothing.

The tests do not catch it because they have one user and one page.

Fix: use `groupResource.getName()` for both the permission check and the returned set, or make `hasPermission` take the `Resource`.

findings.title: Javadoc on the new interface is wrong in places
findings.body:
- `requireManageMembers` (lines 132-135) says it throws when `canManageMembership(GroupModel)` is false. The implementations check `canManageMembers(group)` (GroupPermissions.java:376-380).
- `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` (lines 142-147) says `@return Stream of IDs` but returns `Set<String>`.
- The `canManage()` doc (lines 72-77) says VIEW grants it in V2. That repeats the defect reported in GroupPermissionsV2.java:70.

findings.title: No negative or pagination coverage for the new V2 group evaluation
findings.body:
`testViewGroups` stops at listing. It never checks that an admin with only `view` on all groups is refused `groups().add(...)`, subGroup, update or role mapping. That check would have caught the `canManage()` problem.

The user-search tests use a single member and a single page. There is no test of `users().count()`, or of `first`/`max` with several users where only some are in the permitted group. Those are the paths that use `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`.

contracts.action: Admin user search and count now call auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() unconditionally and place the result in the session attribute UserModel.GROUPS
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous code ran the same call only when !auth.users().canView(). Both V1 and V2 implementations return an empty set when root.users().canView() is true, so the guard moved into the callee.
contracts.before_after: Before: group ids were set only for non-viewers. After: the same, because an empty set is not set as an attribute (UsersResource.java:449-451). toRepresentation still filters with usersEvaluator::canView (UsersResource.java:460), so removing the extra .filter before it only removes a duplicate. The V1 implementation (GroupPermissions.java:298-320) matches the old logic. The V2 implementation (GroupPermissionsV2.java:106-128) returns resource UUIDs.
contracts.visible_effect: For a V2 group-scoped admin the user list is not restricted in the query, and the count endpoint returns 0 for a group-scoped admin.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent wrong results (empty or short pages, count 0), no error.

contracts.action: V2 group manage check used by POST /groups (create top-level group)
contracts.equivalent_path: GroupPermissions.canManage() in V1 (GroupPermissions.java:274-276) checks only the MANAGE_USERS role. GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() (line 65-71) also accepts the VIEW scope.
contracts.before_after: Before: MgmtPermissionsV2 did not override groups(), so the V1 role-only check ran. After: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true for a view-only all-groups permission.
contracts.visible_effect: A view-only admin gets 201/204 from POST /groups instead of 403.
contracts.failure_mode: Authorization bypass, no error or log.

contracts.action: AdminPermissions.registerListener now registers the cleanup listener only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) is enabled at startup
contracts.equivalent_path: Before, the listener was always registered and checked the feature at event time. In V2 mode that check was false, so it did nothing.
contracts.before_after: This matters because GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled throws UnsupportedOperationException (GroupPermissionsV2.java:172-175), and the listener calls it on GroupRemovedEvent (AdminPermissions.java:94). It is safe only if V1 and V2 can never both be enabled. I did not read Profile's versioned-feature handling to confirm that.
contracts.visible_effect: If both could be enabled, deleting a group would throw from the listener.
contracts.failure_mode: Group deletion fails with a 500 error.
contracts.open_question: Does Profile make ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ and ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 mutually exclusive, so isFeatureEnabled(V1) is false whenever V2 is on?

summary: The V2 group permission evaluation has two defects. `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` accepts the VIEW scope, so a view-only admin passes the `requireManage()` check in `POST /groups` (blocker). `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` returns resource UUIDs instead of group ids (fix). That breaks group-restricted user search and makes `users/count` return 0 for group-scoped admins. The V1 refactor looks behaviour-preserving, apart from V1 `canViewMembers` now also honouring MANAGE_MEMBERS. The rest is docs and test-coverage gaps. One contract stays open: whether V1 and V2 can both be enabled, which decides whether the listener change can throw on group deletion. Nothing was built or run.
